coupling: Rank-3 cells keep a packed pointer table allocated as nelems * sizeof(matvar_t *). bab3a6e records internal->num_fields = rank-1 (2) and teaches Mat_VarGetCells to scale a linear index by data_size/sizeof(matvar_t *) only when that field count is greater than 1 and data_size is wider than one pointer; with the packed data_size the scale is skipped, so the commit does not read past the table. 7cf698a teaches Mat_VarGetCell a byte stride: data_size when it is wider than a pointer, otherwise num_fields * sizeof(matvar_t *) when num_fields > 1, otherwise the packed pointer width. On a cell that still has data_size == sizeof(matvar_t *) and num_fields == 0 this is ordinary pointer indexing. 77173f7, after the table is allocated, doubles data_size and nbytes together for a rank-3 cell so nbytes/data_size (what free, print, write, and duplicate walk) stays nelems; nothing in that commit indexes the table by data_size, so the padded sizes do not overflow alone. Composed, Mat_VarGetCell of in-range index 1 of a 2-element rank-3 cell reads 8 bytes past the 16-byte table (stride = data_size = 16). Dropping only the 77173f7 doubling leaves the num_fields stride in Mat_VarGetCell (2 * sizeof(matvar_t *)). Dropping only the bab3a6e num_fields assignment and the Mat_VarGetCells scale leaves the data_size stride in Mat_VarGetCell. Dropping only the 7cf698a stride leaves Mat_VarGetCells scaling index 1 to element 2, because data_size/sizeof(pointer) == 2 and num_fields > 1. Each diff is a no-op on the packed default, and repairing any one of them leaves another pair reachable through the same public cell read.
